stem: Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome presents with advanced periodontal disease in very young children. What is the underlying systemic defect mentioned in the text?

options.text: A lack of salivary flow causing xerostomia.

explanation: The text explicitly links Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome to a neutrophil function defect, leading to severe periodontal destruction and hyperkeratotic skin.
rationale: The defect involves a specific type of white blood cell responsible for fighting infection.

optionExplanations.A: While saliva is important, the primary driver of the severe inflammation in this syndrome is a white blood cell issue.
optionExplanations.B: The text explicitly links Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome to a neutrophil function defect, leading to severe periodontal destruction and hyperkeratotic skin.
optionExplanations.C: Reflux causes acid erosion of the enamel, not the inflammatory periodontal disease seen in this syndrome.
optionExplanations.D: Growth Hormone deficiency is associated with SMMCI, not the aggressive periodontal disease found in Papillon-Lefèvre.
